title: Monday · Reconciliation Walk, decimals and Nevermoor
arrival: Our Reconciliation Walk begins at 9:30. Start with your teacher's morning directions.
note: Working plan: walk and outdoor time can shift. Carry math practice forward if needed. Career content awaits resource review; LST timing awaits confirmation.

blocks.title: Social Studies · TRC Calls to Action
blocks.notes: Connect Orange Shirt Day and residential school learning to changes sought by Survivors and communities. Read one attributed education-related TRC Call to Action, such as #62; paraphrase it and ask who must act, what changes and why. One spoken or written response. Finish before walk prep. NCTR: https://nctr.ca/about/truth-and-reconciliation-commission-of-canada-calls-to-action/
studentSteps: What change does this Call to Action ask for?
Who needs to act, and why does it matter?

blocks.title: Get ready for the walk
blocks.notes: Washroom, clothing, route and expectations. Confirm accessible participation; transition to the start by 9:30.

blocks.title: Reconciliation Walk
blocks.notes: About 20–30 minutes. Follow the school's route and gathering guidance; return around 9:50–10:00.

blocks.title: Outdoor community choices
blocks.notes: Inclusive choice time on usable pavement: chalk, casual ball passing, walking/talking or an accessible game. Check meaningful participation. Flex with return time; no formal PE lesson.
studentSteps: Choose a way to move, play or talk together.
Make room for everyone to join in.

blocks.title: Snack
blocks.notes: Wash hands and snack before recess; flex with return time.

blocks.title: Mathematics · compare and round decimals
blocks.notes: Align digits: 4.386 > 4.368 (hundredths 8 > 6). Round 4.386 to hundredths: thousandths 6 raises 8 to 9, so 4.39. Guide another example. Independent check: 4.305 < 4.350; 7.264 rounds to 7.26. Ask for the deciding digit. Carry practice forward if needed.
studentSteps: Compare decimals one place at a time.
Try the short check on your own.

blocks.title: Language Arts · Nevermoor
blocks.notes: Resume at the actual stopping point. Model a two-sentence response about one character choice with a story detail. Students give one short written, captioned drawing or spoken response; no large assignment.
studentSteps: Share a short response with a story detail.

blocks.title: Career Education · strengths and contribution
blocks.notes: Flexible launch pending review of the Be The Change Earth Alliance booklet. Discuss or note one strength/interest, value or community need, and way to contribute. Connect to careers, responsibility and solutions. Do not imply a pack has been selected or reproduce it.
studentSteps: Name a strength or interest you can use.
How could it help someone or our community?

blocks.title: Classroom community
blocks.notes: Reflection, community building or unfinished learning; revisit inclusion if useful.

blocks.title: Planners, jobs and dismissal
blocks.notes: Planners, jobs, cleanup and dismissal prep.
